Automated Model Briefing

⚠ AI-generated text — may be wrong, incomplete, or overconfident. This is automated commentary on experimental model output, not flight advice and not a weather forecast. It has not been reviewed by a meteorologist.

Overall Assessment — A classic thermal day with dry, cloudless skies, but strong regional southwest flow will make wind the dominant constraint. Lapse rates reach 10 °C/km, producing sharp, strong thermals (peak w* 573 ft/min) that require advanced piloting skill. Site selection is critical: exposed ridge launches and windward sites will see gusty conditions and low-level speed shear, while afternoon wind ramps up steadily across the region.

Site Breakdown

  • Kingsbury Grade: Marginal — Wind crosses from SW, off preferred SE launch direction; increasing to 27 mph by 4pm with bulk shear 36 mph. Best thermal window 9am–11am (w* 258–389 ft/min, ceiling 2654–3431 ft AGL). Sharp thermals (lapse rate 8.7 °C/km) — advanced pilots only.
  • Hallelujah: Favorable — Wind SSW–SW stays within preferred W/SW sector; peak 26 mph. Strong thermals (peak w* 531 ft/min, ceiling 6615 ft AGL). Best window 11am–4pm. Sharp thermals (lapse rate 10.0 °C/km) — advanced pilots only. Watch overdevelopment late (36% of flying hrs).
  • Slide Mountain: Unfavorable — Strong SW wind 28–34 mph all day, crossing from SW against preferred SE launch; hazardous low-level speed shear (8 mph at 240 ft AGL). Thermal window limited by wind, 8am–11am (w* 180–350 ft/min). Lapse rate only 5.2 °C/km.
  • McClellan: Favorable — Wind SSW–SW, well within preferred sector, max 18 mph. Strong thermals (peak w* 564 ft/min, ceiling 6031 ft AGL). Best window 11am–4pm. Sharp thermals (lapse rate 10.0 °C/km) — advanced pilots only. Low-level speed shear present (5 mph).
  • West McClellan: Marginal — Wind SW, mostly within preferred W/SW sector but gusts to 27 mph. Strong thermals (peak w* 498 ft/min, ceiling 5104 ft AGL). Best window 11am–3pm. Sharp thermals (lapse rate 9.5 °C/km) — advanced pilots only. Low-level speed shear present.
  • Peavine Mountain: Unfavorable — Strong SW wind 28–37 mph all day, gusting to 37 mph, with hazardous low-level speed shear. Thermal window limited by wind, 8am–2pm (w* 114–462 ft/min). Not a good choice today.
  • Rainbow Ridge: Favorable — Wind SW, manageable 11–20 mph, though crosses preferred E/NE launch at times. Strongest thermals of the day (peak w* 573 ft/min, ceiling 7121 ft AGL). Best window 11am–3pm. Sharp thermals (lapse rate 10.1 °C/km) — advanced pilots only. Evening drainage switch possible after 6pm.
  • Duck Hill: Marginal — Wind SSE–SW crosses preferred NW launch direction; speeds moderate (10–18 mph). Strong thermals (peak w* 506 ft/min, ceiling 5613 ft AGL). Best window 11am–4pm. Sharp thermals (lapse rate 9.9 °C/km) — advanced pilots only.
  • Daydreams: Favorable — Wind SW–W, well within preferred SW sector, max 28 mph. Moderate thermals (peak w* 276 ft/min, ceiling 3644 ft AGL). Best window 10am–5pm. Sharp thermals (lapse rate 8.2 °C/km). High overdevelopment potential (50% of flying hrs) — watch for cu forming near thermal tops.

Hazards

  • Strong wind / lee rotor zones: SW flow 28–37 mph across Peavine and Slide Mountain creates significant rotor and lee turbulence downwind of major ridgelines.
  • Low-level speed shear: Hazardous shear layers (≥5 mph per layer) present at Slide Mountain (8 mph at 240 ft AGL), Kingsbury Grade (6 mph), West McClellan, McClellan, Peavine, Rainbow Ridge, Duck Hill, and Daydreams — especially dangerous near launch and in the first few hundred feet.
  • Thermal overdevelopment: Hallelujah (36%) and Daydreams (50%) have high risk of cumulus development with LCL close to PBLH — potential for cloud suck or restricted VMC.
  • Sharp, punchy thermals: Lapse rates ≥8.2 °C/km at all sites except Slide Mountain — powerful, tight cores requiring advanced active piloting.
  • Icing risk: Freezing levels around 11,968–14,302 ft MSL; if climb-outs approach cloud base (LCL 6,324–16,707 ft MSL regionally), icing risk exists above the freezing level.

Site Forecast ?Top of Thermals (PBLH) — height of the turbulent mixing layer; thermals typically reach this ceiling.
LCL (Lifted Condensation Level) — altitude where rising air reaches its dew point; theoretical cloud base.
Cloud Base — lowest model level with >10% cloud fraction.
w* — convective velocity scale; higher = stronger thermals (ft/min).
Cloud Cover — max cloud fraction over the column (0–100%).
Wind thresholds: orange = 12 mph, red = 18 mph.
